title: Geometry — The Architecture of Creation: Unit Quiz

questions.question: What are the three undefined terms in Euclidean geometry?
questions.explanation: Point, line, and plane are the three undefined terms — foundational concepts accepted without formal definition upon which all geometric reasoning is built.

questions.question: When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, which angle pairs are congruent?
options: Corresponding angles, alternate interior angles, and alternate exterior angles
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles, alternate interior angles, and alternate exterior angles are all congruent when formed by a transversal crossing parallel lines. Co-interior angles are supplementary (sum to 180°).

questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of any triangle?
questions.explanation: The Triangle Angle Sum Theorem states that the interior angles of any triangle always sum to exactly 180°.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid triangle congruence postulate?
questions.explanation: SSA (Side-Side-Angle) is not a valid congruence postulate because it can produce two different triangles (the ambiguous case). SSS, SAS, ASA, and AAS are all valid.

questions.question: Two triangles are similar. The sides of the smaller triangle are 3, 4, and 5. If the longest side of the larger triangle is 15, what is the scale factor?
questions.explanation: The longest side of the smaller triangle is 5, and the corresponding side of the larger triangle is 15. The scale factor is 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

questions.question: What is the value of π (pi)?
options: An irrational number approximately equal to 3.14159...
A rational number that terminates after 10 decimal places
questions.explanation: Pi is an irrational number — its decimal expansion never terminates and never repeats. It is approximately 3.14159265... Both 3.14 and 22/7 are common approximations but not exact values.

questions.question: An inscribed angle intercepts a semicircle. What is the measure of the inscribed angle?
questions.explanation: By Thales' Theorem, an inscribed angle that intercepts a semicircle (180° arc) is always a right angle (90°), since an inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.

questions.question: What is the volume of a cone with radius 6 cm and height 10 cm?
Can segments of lengths 4, 7, and 12 form a triangle?
options: Yes, because all three lengths are positive
No, because 4 + 7 = 11, which is less than 12
No, because the sides are not equal
questions.explanation: By the Triangle Inequality Theorem, the sum of any two sides must be greater than the third side. Since 4 + 7 = 11 < 12, these segments cannot form a triangle.

questions.question: According to Scripture, what is the Biblical basis for studying and applying geometry?
options: Mathematics was invented by Greek philosophers independent of God
God built mathematical order into His creation, and geometry helps us understand and steward it
Geometry is only useful for building churches
The Bible does not reference any mathematical or geometric concepts
questions.explanation: Scripture reveals that God measured, marked, and designed creation with mathematical precision (Isaiah 40:12, Proverbs 8:27). Studying geometry helps us understand God's orderly creation and equips us to be faithful stewards.
